title: "Last man" is not a law: when it's a red card (DOGSO)

scenes.text: "He was the last man: red card." The law doesn't say that.
Law 12 gives a red card for denying a goal or an obvious goal-scoring opportunity. A deliberate handball counts too.
And from this edition, the referee weighs where the defenders and attackers are, and how many.
But inside the box it changes. If it's a penalty and the defender was trying to play the ball, it's only a yellow.
Holding, pulling, pushing, or no chance of playing the ball? Red card and penalty.
And if the referee plays advantage and the move ends in a goal? Since this year, no card.
It doesn't matter who is last. What matters is the chance you take away.
Save it, and share it with whoever screams red card at every foul.
